title: Chicken, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat is cooked or smoked chicken meat sliced thinly and packaged in vacuum or plastic trays. It is commonly used in sandwiches, salads and snack platters. The product has a mild flavor, tender texture and is a rich source of protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken luncheon meat is often made from skin‑less breast, making it lower in fat than many other deli meats.
Vacuum packaging can extend shelf life up to 30 days without added preservatives.
Smoked versions add a distinctive aroma and further increase shelf stability.
It is popular in diet plans because of its low fat and high protein content.
In some countries the product is classified as a ready‑to‑eat item and does not require further cooking.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat delicacies, chicken luncheon meat contains little saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B6 and niacin, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The meat provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, vital for bones, immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Diet‑friendly
items.content: Low calorie density and high satiety make it a convenient option for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: To enhance flavor the product is often salted; high sodium may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Shelf life after opening
items.content: Once opened, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage can allow pathogenic bacteria to grow, so maintain temperature at 0‑4 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken luncheon meat can be eaten straight from the package, added to sandwiches, salads, wraps, or used in hot dishes such as pasta, omelets or stir‑fries. Thin slices work well as a snack or appetizer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened product in the original packaging in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and consume within a few days. If frozen, it can be kept for up to 2 months, though texture may change.
